title: ApprovalRule
description: Baseline shape of one approval rule, for approval/contracts/rule-representation@0.1.0. A user's rule arrives as a sentence and has to become something a hook evaluates deterministically, before every tool call, outside the model's reach. The condition grammar is closed by construction: an evaluator that cannot be enumerated cannot be reasoned about, and a rule needing a model to evaluate it would put the gate back inside the loop. What this file cannot express is stated by the contract document: that only confirmed rules are passed to the evaluator, that a condition naming a connector, a tool or a property no installed manifest declares is refused at confirmation, and that a statement which cannot be expressed in this grammar is reported as unsupported rather than stored with a weaker condition. This is the product baseline; the shape frozen against an adversarial corpus is approval/contracts/rule-representation@1.0.0 in req-009-rule-ir-hardgate.

id.description: Identity of the rule. A verdict names it, so the approval request can state which rule stopped the call.

statement.description: The user's own words, kept for display. It is what the user is shown when confirming and when reviewing later, and it is never regenerated from the condition.

state.description: A draft rule is the product's reading of what the user meant and has no force; only a confirmed rule reaches the evaluator. A superseded rule is kept because ledger records refer to it.

effect.description: What a match produces. A rule never grants permission: deny outranks require_approval, which outranks allow, and a call matching several rules takes the strongest verdict among them.

testOutcome.description: The outcome of the sample run made after compilation and before confirmation, shown to the user as part of confirming the rule.

scalarValue.description: A value a target property is compared against. Scalars only: a comparison against a structure would need an interpretation, and an interpretation is what the gate exists to avoid.

condition.description: One node of the condition tree. Exactly one variant per node; the grammar is closed, and a statement that needs a variant not listed here is reported as unsupported rather than approximated.

connector.description: A connector identifier. Refused at confirmation when no installed manifest declares it.

tool.description: A tool name. Refused at confirmation when no installed manifest declares it.

irreversible.description: Matches a call the manifest declares has no compensating action, and a write whose prior state could not be read.

objectCountAtLeast.description: Read from the parameter the manifest nominated as its bulk parameter, so the evaluator needs no connector-specific knowledge.

targetProperty.description: Compares against the property values the call would set or the target already holds. A property no connector declares is refused at confirmation, because the condition would otherwise silently never match.

targetOwnedByUser.description: False whenever ownership cannot be determined, because an unknown owner is not the user.
